recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Adding the proposed SNOMED CT map would contradict the published PA resolution, and the duplicate v2/v3 map rendering symptom is already corrected.
issue_request: FHIR-16189 asked to add an authoritative SNOMED CT ConceptMap to the AdministrativeGender value set and remove duplicate v2/v3 AdministrativeGender ConceptMap links. Its final Published/Not Persuasive with Modification resolution rejected the proposed SNOMED CT map as clinical-sex/clinical-gender finding content rather than administrative gender content, and accepted only duplicate v2/v3 map cleanup as a tooling issue.
initial_application: No Jira-keyed source commit for FHIR-16189 was found. The Jira-linked Zulip discussion identifies the duplicate v2/v3 map listing as a tooling/rendering problem over existing bindings.xml data, and git mirror commit 879b2dcd6165efa6d784f86d0e3b3523a461abc3 (svn @14803) changed ConceptMap naming/presentation in the publisher shortly after that report. The Zulip thread confirms the May ballot duplicate rendering was gone.
additional_context: Current core source keeps Patient active and normative, defines the AdministrativeGender code system and value set, and stores the AdministrativeGender mapping data in source/terminologies/bindings.xml. That worksheet has v3 and v2 mapping columns and no SNOMED CT mapping data. Related later issues FHIR-17670, FHIR-24900, and FHIR-29947 concern v2 target exposure, ConceptMap example/rendering review, or relationship-comment rendering, and do not change the FHIR-16189 decision not to add the proposed SNOMED CT map.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit was needed because current source has AdministrativeGender v2/v3 mappings without a SNOMED CT map, and the current rendered value set has one v2 link, one v3 link, and no SNOMED mention.

related_jiras.note: Same AdministrativeGender v2 mapping/rendering family; already represented on the combined branch and supports that current v2 target exposure is correct.
